newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bull flag waves at 116-00 for T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bull flag waves at 116-00 for T-bonds.

text.p: A bull flag formation on daily charts points to gains in September T-bond futures, but Friday's batch of U.S. economic data could change the picture, technical analysts said.
"I am still basically positive on the market," said Miranda Churchill, independent technical analyst in London.
"We have seen a bull flag formation over the past few days. If we can get through 115-14, we can get to 116-00," she added.
September T-bonds were trading at 115-04 at 1019 GMT in automated trade, 6/32 below the Chicago settlement price.
June durable goods orders are due at 1230 GMT.
Orders are expected to have risen 1.4 percent, against May's 0.7 percent drop, according to a Reuters survey.
June existing home sales will be released at 1400 GMT, forecast at 4.19 million against 4.24 million in May.
"The market remains in extremely good shape," said Adrian Sells, director at Crane Investment Analysis in London.
"Once we get the figures out of the way, if 114-28 to 115-00 holds, we can get to 116-00."
The 115-00 level marks a broad area of support on July 22 and is just below the 115-02 July 17 high, before the recent rally, Sells said.
Before reaching 116-00, T-bonds must break through the 115-23 high set on Wednesday, Sells said, which corresponds with the December 5 open on continuation charts.
Beyond 116-00, there is resistance at 116-17 and at 116-28, the continuation chart high from December 3, Churchill said.
If support at 115-02 cracks, the market will back off to 114-13, Churchill said.
"That will hold on a short-term basis."
Sells was more bearish on a drop through initial support.
"If it breaks down, we might get a sharp correction back down to the low 114s."
December Eurodollars look healthy after a strong upmove on July 22, Sells said.
"We will stay in a 94.080 to 94.150 range for today unless we get shock news bringing some new directional moves. On balance the market still looks pretty positive."
